title: Chemistry — Earth and atmosphere
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for KS3 Science (chemistry) (status of the source: authored-reviewed-reverified-2026-10-08). Terms and clues: C8#c15 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; C8#c21 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; C8#c17 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; C8.1#xt2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: C8#q01, C8#q04, C8#q02, C8#q06, C8#q03, C8#x01 (written for the game).

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Weathering
items.clue: The breaking down of rock where it is.

items.label: Atmosphere
items.clue: The layer of gases held around the Earth by gravity.

items.label: Fossil
items.clue: The remains or traces of a living thing preserved in rock.

items.label: Crust
items.clue: The thin, rocky outer layer of our planet, on which we live

questions.stem: What is the Earth's core mainly made of?

options.text: Molten rock called magma
The same rock as the crust
Iron and nickel metal
Water at very high pressure

questions.explanation: Yes. The core is mainly iron with some nickel. The outer core is liquid metal and the inner core is solid metal.

questions.stem: Which statement about the Earth's crust is correct?

options.text: It is the thickest layer of the Earth
It floats on a layer of liquid magma
It is hotter than the rock below it
It is a thin layer of solid rock

questions.explanation: Yes. The crust is solid rock, only about 5–70 km thick. Compared with the whole Earth it is as thin as the skin on an apple.

questions.stem: In the Earth's crust, how are most metals found?

options.text: As lumps or veins of the pure metal
Joined to other elements in compounds
Spread evenly through every kind of rock
As liquid metal that rose from the core

questions.explanation: Yes. Most metals are joined to other elements, often oxygen, in compounds. A rock with enough of a metal compound to be worth extracting is called an ore.

questions.stem: Lava pours out of a volcano. A pupil says this shows that the whole mantle is liquid. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The mantle is a sea of liquid magma
The lava rises up from the Earth's core
Most of the mantle is solid rock
Rock gets colder the deeper you go

questions.explanation: Yes. The mantle is very hot but mostly solid rock, which can flow very slowly over millions of years. Magma forms only where a small amount of rock melts, near the top of the mantle or in the crust.

questions.stem: By mass, iron is the most common element in the whole Earth, but oxygen is the most common in the crust. Which explains this?

options.text: Most of the Earth's iron is in its core
Most of the Earth's iron is in its mantle
Oxygen gas from the air soaks into rocks
Rusting has used up iron in the crust

questions.explanation: Yes. Most of the iron is in the core, deep inside the Earth. The crust is made mostly of compounds of oxygen and silicon, so oxygen is its most common element.

options.text: A layer of liquid rock that the crust floats upon
A layer of liquid iron and nickel around the centre
A thin layer of solid rock forming the surface
A thick layer of mostly solid rock that flows slowly

questions.explanation: The mantle is the thick layer between crust and core: mostly solid rock that can flow very slowly.
